scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Cajun Jitterbug developed as a style of Cajun partner dancing that incorporates swing mechanics into traditional music settings.

It features two main variations: a primary style based on a six-count East Coast Swing two-step pattern, and a cowboy-influenced swing style known under multiple titles, including the Lake Charles Slide, the Cowboy Jitterbug, and the Whiskey River Jitterbug.
While the traditional Cajun Two Step remains the older form, the Cajun Jitterbug evolved to emphasize turns and spins.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers execute the Cajun Jitterbug in partner alignment using open-handed or cross-handed grips held slightly below waist level.
Partners step or walk in time to the music using alternating feet.
The underlying footwork relies on subtle weighting down of one leg—the lead's right foot and follower's left foot—to enable the opposite leg to step and turn freely.
Watch for Hobble Step, Cross-Handed Turn.

Formation: Couples dancing face-to-face with underarm turns and open/cross hand transitions.
